featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited this ENT specialist because I was frequently falling ill with sore throat. During my first visit, she asked me to get a few blood tests, saying she would decide later whether an allergy test was needed. She also prescribed a one-month course of acidity medication. After reviewing the test results, she told me everything looked fine and clearly stated that an allergy test was not required.
However, during the follow-up appointment — since there was no major improvement — she suddenly insisted that I get an allergy test done, contradicting what she had said earlier. When I reminded her of our previous discussion, she argued and refused to acknowledge it.
We went ahead with the allergy test, but only afterward did we start feeling that we were being pushed toward unnecessary procedures. As expected, the results showed allergies to multiple items — which is quite common for most people. She then tried to alarm us by saying she had not seen such “bad reports” in a long time and used this to push an extreme treatment plan. This included completely avoiding certain foods and fruits, and starting immunotherapy for pollen allergies, a very expensive treatment lasting three years.
This was a major red flag for us, and we felt it was more of a money-making strategy than a genuine medical necessity.
When we asked about family planning during immunotherapy, her response was unclear and discouraging. What shocked us most was her unsolicited suggestion that surrogacy is an option if we can afford it — a highly inappropriate comment, especially since she is not a gynecologist and my condition was not severe.
A few months later, another doctor correctly diagnosed me with H. pylori infection, which explained my symptoms — something this ENT specialist failed to identify.
Additionally, the clinic receptionist shared that she had also undergone an allergy test there but chose not to follow the extreme treatment plan and is doing perfectly fine.

My sincere advice: Please do not waste your time or money here. You may eventually be pushed toward allergy testing and expensive long-term immunotherapy, whether it’s truly needed or not.

*Please go for 2nd-3rd opinion*

We consulted Dr Carlton Perreault at Surya Hospital for my 11-month-old son, who had suffered from frequent ear infections (at least three episodes). Our general physician had suggested that we consult an ENT specialist to rule out the need for grommet insertion (myringotomy), if required.

From the beginning, the consultation felt uncomfortable. Dr. Carlton spent considerable time asking about our background and whereabouts probably coz of my wife's accent. When my wife mentioned that we live in Australia and were visiting India for family function and partly because appointments and procedures can be done quicker here, his attitude noticeably changed.

Dr. Carlton then recommended two diagnostic tests for our 11-month-old baby and also suggested a specific diagnostic center. This raised concerns for us. When we checked with multiple other reputed diagnostic centres, they were surprised by these tests being advised for such a young baby and mentioned that these tests are extremely difficult to perform on infants, as the child must remain still for several minutes. We were told by more than one center that these tests are rarely done on babies of this age.

Despite the tests being practically inconclusive, the diagnostic center contacted the doctor, and the results were presented in a way that made it seem like surgery was urgently required.

Dr Carlton explained the condition and the surgical procedure in detail, but at the same time created a sense of urgency and fear, stating that if we delayed the decision, our child could potentially lose his hearing. We requested a few days as we had to travel to our native place. He prescribed antibiotics and pain medication and asked us to decide quickly.

After returning a week later, we sought second opinions from *three senior pediatric ENT specialists* at reputed hospitals. All of them were shocked that such tests were recommended for an infant and strongly disagreed with the suggestion of surgery. They performed a proper examination using an endoscopic camera to inspect the ear canal and eardrum. Their conclusion was consistent: there was only some ear wax, the ears looked healthy, and **no surgery was required at all**.

Based on our experience, I felt extremely uncomfortable and disappointed. It seemed like unnecessary tests and a surgical procedure were being pushed on us, which could have been avoided entirely.

I strongly request parents consulting Dr Carlton to **please seek a second or even third opinion**, especially before agreeing to any surgery for a child.

featured_reviews.name: Dr. Gauri Sawant
featured_reviews.review_text: Dr. Ruchi is a great listener and so calm while examining as well as explaining everything about the treatment. I visited her only once prior personally but a few months later when I had a severe throat infection and I was out of the city, I called her for a consultation, she was very prompt and prescribed me a few medicines via chat, she was super helpful and she also took care of my allergies while prescribing said medicines. I started feeling much much better just after 1-2 doses and she didn't even charge me for this treatment!! (She said since it was online and she didn't see me personally 🥺🥺). I feel very glad to have met Dr. Ruchi, she's one of the best out there!!
